newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban say they advancing on Bamiyan.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban say they advancing on Bamiyan.

text.p: The purist Islamic Taleban milita said its forces had captured the Shibar Pass on Tuesday and had advanced to within five km (3 miles) of the Shi'ite Moslem stronghold of Bamiyan in central Afghanistan.
Mullah Said Mohammad Haqqani, a Taleban spokesman, told the Pakistan-based Pakistan Islamic Press (AIP) service that Taleban fighters "could enter Bamiyan any time this evening."
There was no indepdent confirmation of the reported gain by the Taleban, who have been trying for months to dislodge the Shi'ite opposition Hezb-i-Wahdat faction from the Shibar Pass.
Earlier on Tuesday, an opposition spokesman denied previous claims by the Taleban that they had seized the strategic pass, which leads to Bamiyan and also commands a route to the north.
Hezb-i-Wahdat is one of three main factions in a loose anti-Taleban alliance formed after the Islamic movement captured the capital Kabul in September.
The alliance received a body blow on Monday when a key commander in the forces of northern general adbul rashid dostum launched a pro-Taleban uprising in several northern provinces.
